title: Don't use frames without timestamp for delta time calculations
description:
pcapng allows simple packet blocks (which don't have timestamps),
enhanced packet blocks (which do) and custom blocks (which might
or might not have timestamps, and even if they do have timestamps,
libwiretap might not know about them), and so some records may have
timestamps while others do not.

Do not use frames without timestamps in delta time calculations.
Don't use them as reference frames for time calculations, or for
the previously displayed frame for time calculations, where the
previously displayed frame that actually has a timestamp is used.

Have the various _get_frame_ts functions return null instead of
their ts value (that is currently handled; if records without
timestamps set their abs_ts to the special "unset" value of nstime_t
that could work too, except that isn't currently handled.)

Still allow the GUI to set frames without timestamps as "Time
References", because that does still affect the "Cumulative Bytes"
column, so it's not entirely pointless; unset the reference time
so that the timestamp from the next frame that does have a timestamp
will be used as reference time.

The "previous captured frame" will show a 0 time delta when
the previous frame doeesn't have a timestamp. Perhaps a user
would also want "previous captured frame with a timestamp,"
but we'd have to store that in frame data (adding memory to
that struct.)

Fix #19397

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 51e6f553 - Don't use frames without timestamp for delta time calculations
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12600/diffs?diff_id=815886521&start_sha=c1eaf3aca641be5ce937f4accfc654fa9e033da3)

> Capture file formats like pcapng allow multiple encapsulations and custom blocks, and so some records may have timestamps while others do not.

Encapsulations, such as `LINKTYPE_` values, don't affect whether there's a timestamp.

Custom blocks only have a timestamp if the organization that defines the custom block puts one there, and Wireshark will recognize the time stamp only if we have support for the custom block in wiretap/pcapng.c that adds the timestamp, so they can lack a timestamp.

However, pcapng *also* allows a Simple Packet Block, which lacks a timestamp, so that's *another* way in which a record may lack a timestamp.

> Still allow the GUI to set frames without timestamps as "Time References", because that does still affect the "Cumulative Bytes" column

So does this mean that "Cumulative Bytes" is defined as the number of bytes since the last time reference record?  That's... not obvious.  Perhaps there should be a separate way of marking records as "Cumulative Bytes reference" records.

> it just won't have any effect on timestamps.

That might be a bit surprising.  Should it mean that the reference timestamp is the timestamp of the first record *after* the"Time Reference" record that has a timestamp?

> That's... not obvious.  Perhaps there should be a separate way of marking records as "Cumulative Bytes reference" records.

Yes, perhaps, because it really isn't obvious. (Also, I noticed while looking into this that the part that the `cum_bytes` member of the frame data struct is a 32 bit integer, which is not necessarily sufficient now. Perhaps it's possible to rearrange the members when changing that to 64 bit so it doesn't increase the size of the struct.)

> Should it mean that the reference timestamp is the timestamp of the first record after the "Time Reference" record that has a timestamp?

Hmm, perhaps so? That wouldn't be too hard to implement, just set the "reference frame" to NULL instead of ignoring it, ans then the next record would pick it up. That might make more sense.

added 3 commits
  • 51e6f553...a4527fa0 - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 9745a573 - Don't use frames without timestamp for delta time calculations
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12600/diffs?diff_id=815940170&start_sha=51e6f553664145232d333ebb3060002bd9ceb87d)

Made the change as you suggested, I think that makes more sense, thanks. Now marking a record without a timestamp as a "Time Reference" will cause the timestamp of the next record after it with a timestamp to be used as the reference time (while still resetting the Cumulative Bytes counter.)

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12600/diffs?diff_id=816008708&start_sha=9745a5733aae383331fe94516576fa8ef89f0d1c)

added 5 commits
  • d86c3c06...8da773da - 4 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • f1f6c136 - Don't use frames without timestamp for delta time calculations
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12600/diffs?diff_id=816026584&start_sha=d86c3c064ff18a9860f01ff6e87a64bd1e3b388d)

Thank you for the link, @johnthacker.

I guess this merge request did not make it into the most recent windows build v4.2.0rc3, in which [my issue](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/17923#note_857335308) has not been resolved yet.

Which build / release will contain this merge request?

Using the example-pcapng-46254-block.pcapng, I have created [example_missing_timestamp.pcapng](/uploads/b050696e6cc8491ef195e92d516cdf0d/example_missing_timestamp.pcapng).

```
tshark.exe -r example_missing_timestamp.pcapng -q -z io,stat,-1

=======================================
| IO Statistics                       |
|                                     |
| Duration: 1691743357.4 secs              |
| Interval: 1691743357.4 secs              |
|                                     |
| Col 1: Frames and bytes             |
|-------------------------------------|
|                    |1               |
| Interval           | Frames | Bytes |
|-------------------------------------|
|     0.0 <> 1691743357.4 |      3 |  1697 |
=======================================
```
Hi @mstv, I made a MR to get this in 4.2. It should be able to get in the next release.
Thank you! It works with v4.2.0.
